status: partial prepared implementation; not published or versioned as 1.72
finding: Gorilla processes ping/pong inside ReadMessage, so accounting only returned data messages leaves control traffic outside the shared read-pump budget.
changes: Charge incoming ping and pong against the same connection-local300-initial,200/second budget as data messages, before executing their handlers.
Keep normal default ping echo and the existing pong read-deadline renewal. Excess sends close1008 and terminates the reader without logging untrusted control payloads or creating an account/IP ban.
Suppress the expected local frame-limit error from general read-error logging; individual message authorization and malformed-message limits remain separate.

checks.negativeSockets: Two actual loopback WebSocket cases consume300 data messages then verify the next ping or pong receives1008 and ends the read with the local policy error. A fixed clock isolates shared-budget behavior from scheduler/refill timing.
checks.positiveSocket: Actual ping echo, custom pong deadline handler and subsequent ordinary data response remain functional, and all three consume the shared budget.
checks.retainedUnitChecks: Initial burst, refill, rewind rejection, malformed isolation and deterministic ordinary mixed traffic remain passing.

limits: Loopback handler tests are not a new production-binary/database/session acceptance, real-player load, high-latency simulation or edge/global connection protection.
The earlier dependency-frame receipt retains its own binary hash and test scope; it does not implicitly cover this follow-up source.
Movement/cast authority, private-state boundaries, broader secret/dependency exposure and connection admission still require completion before1.72 closes.
